params.body:
## What

The trends on the site "still sound a bit off". The main reason is not the wording: **the site shows 144 trends that are 48 ideas**, measured with the fold check's own rule (patterns or signals overlapping by half). Thirteen versions of the curator economy, ten of peer trust around institutions, nine of the algorithm, then 9, 7, 7, 7, 5. Read one by one each is fine; read as a list it is one idea told nine ways.

The model already has what this needs, in three pieces that never met:

1. **The fold check** (since about 11 September) stops a twin at birth. It works: none of the 96 twins on the site is younger than that. But it only looks forward, and the public set was approved in July and August, one proposal per mail.
2. **The site shows a chain once.** `listShowcaseInsights` follows `superseded_by` to the head and deduplicates. So linking twins is enough; the site needs no change.
3. **A refinement** (`supersedes`) is the writer's own "this refines X". But it wrote only the new side, while the site and the refinement eval (`evals.mjs`, `WHERE o.superseded_by = m.id`) read the old side. All 25 refinements in the store left their original standing beside them.

## How

- `insight-economy.mjs`: `isTwin` (the fold check's rule, `TWIN_LINE = 0.5`, now shared with `findOverlap`), `twinGroups` (a twin of a twin joins the group), `headOf` (strongest evidence, then most signals, then newest) and `linkTwins`, which marks the others the way consolidate marks what it merged (`superseded_by`, status `superseded`), folds their signals into the head so the card that stays carries all the evidence, logs it, and does nothing on a second run.
- `bin/fold-twins.mjs`: **a dry run by default.** It lists every group with the head it keeps and what it folds, as markdown with `--out`, for an editor to choose from. `--head <id>` picks another head, `--keep <id>` takes a member out of its group (a twin of a twin can pull in a neighbouring idea), `--apply` links.
- `writeInsight` links a refinement both ways, and a one-time migration (`refinements-linked-2026-09-23`) links the existing ones.

## Checked on a copy of the live store

On the box, against a `.backup` copy of `signals.db` in a temporary folder (removed afterwards; the live store was not touched): the migration linked **21** of the 25 refinements (4 originals had already been replaced by something else and were left alone), and the dry run printed **144 public trends, 48 ideas, 28 groups, 96 versions to fold**. The list is attached in the session, not applied.

## Tests

`test/twins.test.mjs`: the rule, grouping, the head, that the site shows a group once after linking with the evidence of all members (checked by mutation: dropping the evidence fold fails it), that a second run does nothing, and that a refinement marks its original. `insight-economy.test.mjs` had pinned that a refinement leaves the fresh stock unchanged, which held only because the original was never retired; it now pins that the original leaves the stock, as a merge's originals already do, and the refinement gets its own target so it no longer collides with the fold test.

## After the merge

Nothing changes on the site until someone runs `--apply`. The migration runs once on deploy and links the 21. Then: the dry run's list goes to Maarten, who picks heads and keeps apart what is really its own idea.
params.title: One trend per idea: twins linked to their head, refinements linked both ways
